How Kubernetes, helm and these images behave: A StatefulSet with updateStrategy RollingUpdate replaces its pods one at a time from the highest ordinal, deleting each old pod before it creates its replacement (there is no surge); with partition N, pods with an ordinal below N keep the old version; with OnDelete no pod is replaced until someone deletes it. A replacement pod mounts the same PVCs from volumeClaimTemplates. A pod's emptyDir volumes and its container filesystem are deleted together with the pod; only data on a PersistentVolume outlives it. When a PVC is deleted, its PersistentVolume and the data on it are deleted if the reclaimPolicy is Delete; with Retain the volume and its directory stay on the node (Released). A PVC that a pod still mounts is not removed when it is deleted: it stays Terminating, and the pod keeps using it, until no pod mounts it any more; then it is removed. Deleting a StatefulSet or scaling it down keeps the PVCs created from its volumeClaimTemplates, unless its persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy says Delete for that case (whenDeleted or whenScaled). A StatefulSet pod that is deleted is recreated with the same name and the same PVC name; if that PVC is gone, a new empty one is created. The postgres image applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD only when it initializes an empty data directory; a data directory that already holds a database keeps its users, passwords and pg_hba.conf. An empty data directory is initialized as a new, empty database.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
